newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrafina says has 9 pct in Suez/Lyonnaise group.
newsitem.headline: Electrafina says has 9 pct in Suez/Lyonnaise group.

text.p: Belgian holding company Electrafina, a unit of Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL), said on Tuesday it owned about nine percent in the share capital of the merged French group Suez/Lyonnaise.
The merger between Compagnie de Suez and French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux is to be completed later this year.
Belgian financier Albert Frere, chairman of Electrafina and head of group GBL, told Electrafina shareholders Electrafina so far had invested about 35 billion francs in the Suez group.
"It is clear that we have confidence in the Suez/Lyonnaise management and its startegy," he said.
The merged French group wants to become a world leader in colective services, notable energy, water and waste management.

Asked what his further plans were with the stake, he gave no indications. "It is too soon to speculate about the future of this asset. Like all our assets it could in time generate a capital gain for us, which is our aim."
